bets.name: Wrong-fitment returns down by a third

guardrails.name: Added run cost per month once live

text: Long-tail and foreign VINs stay dependent on the vendor
Right shape for marketplace, but run cost breaches the 15k hard limit.
receipt: Vendor reply of 1 Dec sets the fee at 0.09, not the 0.08 the draft uses (evidence/vendor-reply.md; options.yaml note). At 0.09 run cost is 17,775 a month (our arithmetic, Engineering agrees), a breach of the 15,000 hard limit the owner confirmed in answers.yaml. Return falls from opening because payback month 9 was built on 0.08 and 25% adoption. Growth is lower than opening because the 9% year-1 share is not reached in the phased schedule. Strategy fit stays high because phase 2 keeps S-009 and the marketplace path open, but the phase 2 date is not yet in the files.

text: Phase 1 can ship for spring; the draft still breaches run cost.
receipt: Opening ttm 85 assumed a 6-week MVP. Engineering round 1 (section 1) puts phase 1 at 8 weeks, range 6 to 10, so value lands late January to mid-March, which is still inside the window if the build starts in early December. Experience 85 to 58: phase 1 leaves the dropdown on the S-009 old IDs, so the 'your vehicle' result and the filters can disagree (Engineering round 1, section 1; my round 1 challenge). Adoption 75 to 62: the draft has no fix for run cost at 0.09 (17,775 a month), so the fix is a traffic cap or a recorded breach (Engineering round 1, section 6).

text: Phased draft is optimistic at 12 weeks; phase 2 must be dated.
receipt: Moved from opening: arch_fit 88 to 80, debt 85 to 70, capacity 80 to 62, reversibility 85 to 82. Receipts: effort 12 is the optimistic end of my 14 point (range 12 to 18), since S-009 is priced at 8 weeks in memory/shortcuts.yaml and phase 2 as drafted (4 weeks) is short of my 6-week estimate; S-009 is fixed only in phase 2, which is undated; phase 1 keeps the selector on supplier IDs, so two ID schemes run in spring (Product, debate r1). Run cost at 0.08 is 16,800, a guardrail breach outside my mandate.

text: Offer terms at 0.08 block the privacy copy we need; redo.
receipt: Opening hybrid view held, but the draft is superseded: the 24 November reply moves the fee to 0.09 and sets processor-only terms with 30-day retention (Legal, Executive, Engineering). Data says the 3.8% to 4.8% gap includes self-selection, so my 21% cost-per-order upper bound is withdrawn.

text: Offer terms keep our VINs 24 months with reuse; not signable as drafted.
receipt: Changed from opening (hybrid on signable terms, pre-check and holdout in place). Draft is priced on the offer as sent: 24-month VIN retention with service-improvement use, so our storage precondition is not met; no post-termination licence either. Ownership held at 55, not lower, because vendor IDs sit only in a mapping table. Measurement is 75: holdout flag and logging are in phase 1, but the +0.6 pt rule on VIN users cannot be read from a blended holdout (Product: about 0.25 pt at 25% entry). I concede the rule and move it to intent-to-treat. Quality 60: no pre-check, no abstain rule. Phase 2 is undated, so red line own_core_data holds only if phase 2 is dated before the marketplace connector starts.

text: Offer terms are stale; no signature at 0.08 without reply terms.
receipt: Opening view was hybrid on a processor-only contract. The draft's 0.08 fee is the offer's price, and the 24 November reply prices processor-only terms at 0.09. Signing 0.08 therefore means signing the offer's 24-month retention and reuse clause, which the reply withdraws. That breaks lawful_basis (GDPR Art 28(3)(a)). Lifts only if the draft is rewritten on the reply terms, which makes it hybrid_terms_conditional.

text: hybrid_phased_draft: rejected, red lines broken_promise, guardrail_breach, lawful_basis; guardrails added run cost per month once live

items.name: Vehicle identification by VIN
items.label: Buy: vendor API, direct integration, on 24 November vendor terms

bets.name: Wrong-fitment returns down by a third

guardrails.name: Added run cost per month once live

text: Search, cart and returns keyed to the vendor's vehicle IDs
Inside guardrails and fastest, but locks out the marketplace bet.
receipt: Owner confirmed in answers.yaml that the marketplace bet is firm and not to be traded for a cheaper integration. S-040 blocks marketplace, with an 8 to 10 week remap (72k to 90k) later and no leverage on price (candidates.yaml), so strategy fit falls well below my opening. Buy stays inside all three guardrails at 0.09 (one-off 36k, run cost 10,275, payback month 4), so return is strong. Growth is the best of the three: 10% of the 12M goal in year 1 and a two-month time to value. The 1,500 run cost is unsourced in the case.

text: Fastest for customers, but owner has ruled out the marketplace bet.
receipt: Ttm 85 to 88: 4 team-weeks and 2 months to value, so the customer value lands before phase 1 would (session business_case.yaml, buy_terms). Experience 85 to 80: one ID scheme from day one, so no disagreement between 'your vehicle' and filters; a later remap of garage profiles would be customer-visible (my round 1 pros and cons). Adoption 75 to 78: the run cost sits inside the 15,000 limit on the case figures, so no traffic cap is forced. Buy is ruled out by the owner's marketplace answer (Executive round 1, section 2). That is outside this mandate, so it is not scored here, and it is why Product does not pick buy.

text: Blocks marketplace via S-040 and deepens S-009; red line.
Fastest parity, but no advantage and no owned retention channel.
receipt: Withdrew my buy fallback. An 8-week owned layer lands before mid-March, and buy alone blocks the marketplace through S-040 (Engineering red line), so 'works for every seller' stays off the table. Legal adds a mapping-licence gate for buy exit. Buy keeps the earliest parity, which is its only competitive edge; its per-order cost is no lower than hybrid's and it has no owned retention channel.

text: Keys search, cart and returns to vendor IDs; breaks own_core_data.
receipt: Changed from opening: search, cart, order history, returns and the planned garage key would be keyed to vendor IDs (S-040), and marketplace sellers cannot match to our vehicle_id. That breaks own_core_data, so ownership is not a trade-off. Measurement 70: earliest readout (value from month 2), but the 4 team-weeks name no instrumentation or holdout, so logging must be added inside them. Quality 55: no own mapping table and no abstain layer; same vendor claim of 98.5% and 95% coverage, untested on our VINs. Not a red line on measurable, as long as the holdout is built.

text: Buy exit is blocked until we hold a post-termination mapping licence.
receipt: The reply's processor-only terms remove the data clause that drove my buy red line, so buy no longer breaks lawful_basis once the DPA is signed. Contract still fails: no licence to keep vendor-keyed mapping after termination, so exit means a remap of 8 to 10 weeks (S-040) with no price leverage. Claims score lower: 'works for every seller' cannot be substantiated under buy, and the 98.5% precision is the vendor's own test set.

text: buy_reference: rejected, red lines no_strategic_blocker, own_core_data; new risk to Marketplace, year end

text: Signable only if the volume tier is written; not in the reply.
receipt: The volume tier and minimum-fee ramp that would clear 15,000 are not in the vendor reply (evidence/vendor-reply.md; options.yaml). Without them the flat 0.09 model breaches by 2,775 a month, so the option fails the hard limit on the terms in writing. If the tier is refused, the fallback caps VIN-entry traffic at about 66,667 lookups, which cuts about a third of base lookups and lowers growth below opening. The 14-week Engineering point (range 12 to 18) leaves about 10 weeks for marketplace and eu-markets, so strategy fit is below the draft. Return is lower than the draft because one-off cost is 126k and payback is not re-run at 0.09.

text: No signature without volume terms; a traffic cap then costs customers adoption.
receipt: Ttm 85 to 65: the variant depends on a volume tier and ramp that the vendor reply does not contain, and the executive will not sign without them (Executive round 1, section 7). Signature could slip past mid-February. Market window not marked broken, because a traffic cap lets phase 1 ship without the tier. Adoption 75 to 58: without the tier, the fallback caps VIN entry at about 66,700 lookups a month, about 17% adoption (Engineering round 1, section 6). Experience 85 to 55: a cap turns VIN entry on for some customers and off for others, and phase 1 keeps the two ID schemes.

text: Honest effort; holds only if written tiers and a named owner land.
receipt: Moved from opening: arch_fit 88 to 80, debt 85 to 72, capacity 80 to 66, reversibility 85 to 70. Receipts: effort 14 point is the honest figure (58% of 24 weeks at point, 75% at top of range), and phase 2 at about 6 weeks closes S-009 on a realistic plan; reversibility falls because the 24-month term exits only after month 12 plus 3 months' notice (earliest month 15, Legal), and the post-termination mapping licence is not yet in writing. Run cost at flat 0.09 is 17,775 unless a volume tier is written; the tier and minimum-fee ramp are not in the vendor reply, so this option is conditional.

text: Parity by March; claim matched parts only; campaign after signed tier.
receipt: Story up from opening: processor-only terms, 30-day retention and no reuse let us state the retention window honestly (Legal, Engineering). Legal also replaced 'exact vehicle' with 'parts matched to your vehicle'. Acquisition down from opening: the 0.09 fee raises cost per order, and the owner's garage and CRM channels moved to phase 2, so spring has no retention lever. Campaign spend waits for a signed tier or an agreed traffic cap, so a rationed feature is never advertised.

text: Acceptable only with post-termination mapping licence and dated phase 2.
receipt: Reply of 24 November (evidence/vendor-reply.md) removes the 24-month retention and reuse and allows caching for our customers, so ownership rises from the draft to 70. Still open: a post-termination licence to keep mapped results and bulk export on exit (Legal section 4); without them exit is blocked, so not 85. Measurement held at 75 for the same intent-to-treat correction as the draft. Quality held at 60: the 2,000-VIN pre-check and abstain-below-threshold rule are not written into this option. If both are written into phase 1, I would score 75. The 0.06 volume tier is a run-cost question for Executive, not scored here.

text: Reply terms are signable once DPA, audit, breach and mapping licence land.
receipt: Met on paper since opening: processor-only terms, 30-day retention, no reuse, 5% cap at 24 months, month-12 exit with 3 months' notice (vendor reply, 24 November). Below opening because the reply is silent on liability cap, audit, breach notice (24 to 48 hours), post-termination licence for the mapping and results, deletion on instruction and SLA, and the DPA is attached but not reviewed. Veto is a signature gate: no live VIN lookup before a signed DPA.
